localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10 brings the first signs of the fall transition to Choctawhatchee Bay, with water at 87°F and bait schools — particularly greenies and pogies — moving from open water into bayous, flats, bridge pilings, and the East Pass. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reports that slot redfish and speckled trout are holding around grass flats, sandy pockets, docks, and deeper cuts, while bull redfish and jack crevalle are actively feeding on bait schools around Rocky Bayou, Boggy Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and the East Pass. The full fall mullet-driven slot redfish push is expected to ramp up in the second or third week of September, so conditions should only improve for bay inshore anglers over the coming weeks.
